result:
Rebase rarely fits a shared branch. It rewrites commits, so teammates' clones diverge from the rewritten history and force-pushes can overwrite their work.

Rebase is safe when:
- Only you have commits on the branch, or the team agrees to it.
- Nobody else has pulled the commits you're rewriting.
- You're rebasing your local work onto the updated upstream before pushing (`git pull --rebase`). Those commits aren't public yet.
- You're cleaning up your own unpushed commits.

Use merge when:
- Others push to the branch.
- You're integrating the shared branch with `main`. Merge preserves history and needs no force-push.

If you must rebase a shared branch, announce it first. Push with `--force-with-lease`, not `--force`, and have teammates run `git fetch` followed by `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` or `git pull --rebase`.
